I searched CPRD for "eczema", "atopic", "atopy", "dermatitis", "neurodermatitis", "Besnier", "prurigo" and "eczematous", and looked up the code ranges M11, M111, M12z and Myu2.

## Atopic eczema codelist

### Core codes (definite atopic eczema)

| Read code | Term |
|:---|:---|
| M11 | Atopic dermatitis |
| M111 | Atopic dermatitis/eczema |
| M111-98 | Atopic eczema/dermatitis |
| M111-97 | Dermatitis/eczemas NOS |
| M111-99 | Dermatitis/eczemas |
| M11z | Atopic dermatitis NOS |
| M11z-99 | Atopic eczema/dermatitis NOS |
| M112 | Infantile eczema |
| M113 | Flexural eczema |
| M114 | Allergic (intrinsic) eczema |
| M115 | Besnier's prurigo |
| M117 | Atopic neurodermatitis |

### Broader codes (general eczema codes, often included in validated UK atopic eczema algorithms)

| Read code | Term |
|:---|:---|
| M12z1 | Eczema |
| M12z1-99 | Chronic Eczema |
| Myu22 | Exacerbation of eczema |
| M12z2 | Infected eczema |
| M12z4 | Erythrodermic eczema |
| Myu2 | [X]Dermatitis and eczema |
| A540 | Eczema herpeticum - Kaposi's varicelliform eruption (a complication that almost only happens with atopic eczema) |

### Codes I left out on purpose
- **Other types of eczema:** seborrhoeic (M101 family), contact/irritant/allergic contact (M12x family), varicose/gravitational (G831, G832, M1y2), discoid/nummular (M119, M12z1-1, M1y0), asteatotic (M11A), pompholyx/vesicular hand eczema (M252, M2522), hand eczema (M12z3), pustular eczema (M102-1, M07y-1), infectious eczematoid dermatitis (M102), ear and eyelid eczema, and eczema of nipple (26C4).
- **Other conditions in the M11 range:** napkin/nappy rash (M110 family), infantile seborrhoeic dermatitis and cradle cap (M118 family), and diffuse/Brocq's neurodermatitis (M116 family, M1831).
- **Codes that don't show current disease:** history (14F1 H/O: eczema), family history (12H1, 12Z4), referral (8HTu), general atopy (SN533) and Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome (C3912-1).

**How to use it:** For high specificity, use the core codes only. For high sensitivity, add the broader codes. Many UK studies define atopic eczema as an eczema diagnosis code plus at least two eczema treatment prescriptions on separate days. That gives a more accurate case definition when you use the generic "Eczema" codes.

## Atopic eczema codelist

### Core codes (definite atopic eczema)

| Read code | Term |
|:---|:---|
| M11 | Atopic dermatitis |
| M111 | Atopic dermatitis/eczema |
| M111-98 | Atopic eczema/dermatitis |

| M111-99 | Dermatitis/eczemas |

| M11z-99 | Atopic eczema/dermatitis NOS |
| M112 | Infantile eczema |
| M113 | Flexural eczema |
| M114 | Allergic (intrinsic) eczema |
| M115 | Besnier's prurigo |
| M117 | Atopic neurodermatitis |

### Broader codes (general eczema codes, often included in validated UK atopic eczema algorithms)

| Read code | Term |
|:---|:---|
| M12z1 | Eczema |
| M12z1-99 | Chronic Eczema |
| Myu22 | Exacerbation of eczema |
| M12z2 | Infected eczema |
| M12z4 | Erythrodermic eczema |
| Myu2 | [X]Dermatitis and eczema |
| A540 | Eczema herpeticum - Kaposi's varicelliform eruption (a complication that almost only happens with atopic eczema) |

### Codes I left out on purpose
- **Other types of eczema:** seborrhoeic (M101 family), contact/irritant/allergic contact (M12x family), varicose/gravitational (G831, G832, M1y2), discoid/nummular (M119, M12z1-1, M1y0), asteatotic (M11A), pompholyx/vesicular hand eczema (M252, M2522), hand eczema (M12z3), pustular eczema (M102-1, M07y-1), infectious eczematoid dermatitis (M102), ear and eyelid eczema, and eczema of nipple (26C4).
- **Other conditions in the M11 range:** napkin/nappy rash (M110 family), infantile seborrhoeic dermatitis and cradle cap (M118 family), and diffuse/Brocq's neurodermatitis (M116 family, M1831).
- **Codes that don't show current disease:** history (14F1 H/O: eczema), family history (12H1, 12Z4), referral (8HTu), general atopy (SN533) and Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome (C3912-1).

**How to use it:** For high specificity, use the core codes only. For high sensitivity, add the broader codes. Many UK studies define atopic eczema as an eczema diagnosis code plus at least two eczema treatment prescriptions on separate days. That gives a more accurate case definition when you use the generic "Eczema" codes.

### Core codes: specific to atopic eczema
| Read code | Term |

### Broader codes: unspecified eczema or complications
In primary care, unspecified "eczema" codes usually mean atopic eczema, so published atopic eczema codelists often include them. Whether you include them depends on how sensitive versus specific you want the list to be.
